Round Keyboard Lab

Thirteen ways to type on 35 mm of round glass, all operable at 1:1 scale below so the feel can be compared before any C is written. Panel #1 is the proposed v2 hybrid (user direction 2026‑11‑02): 12 coarse press sectors sized to their letter groups — every letter owns an equal 13.8° (360/26) of the ring, so 2‑letter sectors span 27.7° and the two 3‑letter sectors 41.5° — a reveal that on touch‑down overlays the inner circle (r150–226) showing only the pressed sector's options on one radius, a centre preview of the selected letter (DTMF‑style) until release commits and the full entry re‑appears, 4 × 60° shift keys on the top arc, ⊗ commit at the bottom, centre tap = backspace — instant reveal, no full-screen redraw. The rest keep the firmware's geometry (doc §7.13) and the report's evidence rows (research of 2026‑11‑01).

Evidence, full 37‑source list and the cost model: docs/research/circular-keyboard-alternatives.md (commit 9f5a2cf). Key primary sources: C‑QWERTY (2020), Crownboard (CHI 2023 PDF), WrisText (CHI 2018), Tap’nSwipe (IJHCI 2025), smartwatch QWERTY trace/tap WPM (SAGE 2019), T9 (Wikipedia), in‑car dial study (Brewster, CHI 2017).

Open questions the research leaves: (1) C‑QWERTY’s QWERTY‑vs‑alphabetical effect size (full text bot‑blocked); (2) what the sweep actually feels like on the CST9217 — the pending real‑glass device check; (3) multi‑tap timeout tuning (500/700/900 ms) needs a real‑glass micro‑study. This page mocks the interaction, not the benchmark.
